once_through.title: Water intake
once_through.general_explanation: Water is withdrawn to supply cooling.
unknowns: Exact intake geometry, flow and organism capture are not provided by monthly temperatures.

once_through.title: Heat transfer
once_through.general_explanation: Cooling water takes up heat while steam is cooled back into liquid water.
unknowns: Monthly inlet/outlet averages do not show instantaneous heat flow or the path of one droplet.

once_through.title: Discharge and mixing
once_through.general_explanation: Water returns to a receiving water body, where further mixing depends on local conditions.
unknowns: No downstream temperature map, mixing distance or safety conclusion is available.

recirculating.title: Make-up water
recirculating.general_explanation: Water can be added to replace losses from a cooling loop.
unknowns: The data do not establish the exact make-up source or the amount lost.

recirculating.title: Heat transfer
recirculating.general_explanation: Water circulating through cooling equipment receives heat and can be cooled for reuse.
unknowns: Loop temperatures do not describe every heat exchange or any ecosystem effect.

recirculating.title: Cooling, reuse and any release
recirculating.general_explanation: Towers or ponds can remove heat before reuse; any released water must be assessed separately.
unknowns: Do not animate the entire circulating flow as a direct river discharge; release details are not established here.

unknown.title: Water intake — educational example
unknown.general_explanation: Some cooling designs withdraw water; other designs use different water sources or air cooling.
unknowns: The selected system type and actual intake are not confirmed for this example.

unknown.title: Heat transfer — educational example
unknown.general_explanation: Heat is removed from the power cycle by cooling equipment; the design determines how.
unknowns: The drawing does not establish the selected plant’s equipment or cooling-water route.

unknown.title: Reuse or discharge — educational example
unknown.general_explanation: Depending on the design, water may be cooled and reused, released, or partly lost by evaporation.
unknowns: This is not evidence that the selected plant uses a once-through river system or forms a particular thermal plume.

limitations: The drawing does not track an actual droplet or depict the real pipe layout.
No plume shape, travel time, population effect or safety verdict is calculated.
Historical cooling codes are not a current engineering inspection; mixed/unknown codes remain educational.

research_notes: PUDL code definitions and USGS explanation read on 2026-11-15. Type families only, not subvariant geometry.
Historical operator page3-3 says upriver return; NRC2019 draft page3-3 says downstream. Direction/distance deliberately not used; needs site review.
No labels from a fictional ecological-safety model and no lifetime/health inference are used.
